issues.legal_issue: A statute enacted by a state legislature that was functioning at the constitutional transition is not invalid merely because that legislature may have been defectively constituted under the earlier arrangement.
material_facts: The assembly was functioning as the state's legislature immediately before the Constitution came into force.
The election of some assembly members had not strictly followed the procedure prescribed by the earlier covenant, and the challengers argued that this defect made the assembly an usurping body.
The assembly enacted the challenged statute after the Constitution came into force.
The appeals challenged the statute's validity on the ground that the assembly had not been validly constituted.
issues.conclusion: The assembly's possible defective constitution did not invalidate the statute. The appeals were dismissed on this ground.
issues.legal_principle: Article 385 of the Constitution recognizes the body or authority functioning as the legislature of a corresponding Indian State immediately before the Constitution came into force and gives it the powers and duties of the legislature under the Constitution, until the new legislature is constituted. The Court treated Articles 379 and 382 as reflecting the same transitional approach: the Constitution recognized bodies actually functioning without requiring an inquiry into whether they had been validly constituted under the prior arrangements. Accordingly, an assembly exercising powers under Article 385 could enact a statute whose validity could not be challenged on the basis of defects in its earlier formation.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_state_statute and legislature_functioned_at_transition and statute_enacted_after_transition and legislature_formation_defective

predicates.appeal_challenging_state_statute: A party appealed while challenging the validity of a state statute.
predicates.legislature_functioned_at_transition: A body was actually functioning as the state's legislature immediately before the new constitutional order began.
predicates.statute_enacted_after_transition: The functioning legislature enacted the statute after the new constitutional order began.
predicates.legislature_formation_defective: The legislature had been formed in a manner that did not strictly comply with the rules of the prior arrangement.

issues.definition: When a challenged state statute was enacted after the constitutional transition by a legislature that was actually functioning at that transition, a defect in the legislature's formation does not produce the output that the statute is invalid on that ground.
